title: Build a circuit breaker in Go — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a circuit breaker: turn 1 closed state (count failures), turn 2 open state (reject calls), turn 3 half-open recovery.

task_spec.prompt: Implement the closed-state logic in `Call()` in `cb/cb.go`: when the circuit is closed, call fn(), track failures. If fn() returns an error increment c.failures; if it succeeds reset c.failures to 0. When c.failures reaches c.maxFailures, transition to StateOpen and record c.openUntil = time.Now().Add(c.resetTimeout). Return any error from fn(). Run `go test ./...`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now add the open-state logic: at the start of Call(), check if c.state == StateOpen. If time.Now().Before(c.openUntil) return ErrOpen immediately. Otherwise transition to StateHalfOpen and allow the call through. Run `go test ./...` and fix any failures.

Final step: add half-open recovery — when in StateHalfOpen and fn() succeeds, reset to StateClosed with zero failures. If fn() fails in StateHalfOpen, go back to StateOpen and reset the timer. Run `go test ./...` — all 6 tests must pass.
success_criteria: Closed state counts failures and opens at maxFailures
Success in closed state resets failure count
Open state returns ErrOpen immediately without calling fn
After resetTimeout, circuit transitions to HalfOpen
Successful probe in HalfOpen closes the circuit
Failed probe in HalfOpen re-opens the circuit
